_comment: INFORMATIVE — REPEATABLE TEMPLATE. The same composition every run, new content each time: prompt → suspense → reveal, ×N. Generalised from a production config; every project-specific value is a <placeholder>. Build the composition ONCE (Remotion or ffmpeg), then feed it configs forever. See references/formats.md §3a.
_startingPoint: A proven starting point, not a spec. The cadence, the item count and the reveal timing worked for someone else's audience — tweak them for yours, one variable per experiment. references/formats.md covers running a format that isn't here.

meta.title: <slug-for-this-video>
meta.concept: <the ONE theme of this video — every item belongs to it>

template._comment: Fixes the look so a config only has to carry content. One template per variant you run (per language, per category, per audience) — a new variant is a copy of this file with these fields changed.

background.query: <a scene that MATCHES this video's theme — food content over a food scene. A mismatched backdrop looks broken even when nobody can say why.>
background.fallback: <a curated on-brand pool to fall back to when the stock search misses — a wrong-topic image is worse than a repeat>
background.motion: slow zoom + pan, so a still can carry 60 seconds

template.character: <shared/assets/ — an optional recurring figure that makes the series recognisable>
template.badges: <optional row of small images that signal the category at a glance>
template.brandColour: <hex — used for the reveal, so the payoff is always the same colour>
template.fonts: <extra faces needed if your content isn't Latin script; empty otherwise>
template.outro: <the follow line, e.g. 'Follow for one of these every day'>

cadence._comment: Derived timing — the reason a config is only content. gap = seconds per item, guess = the suspense beat before the reveal.

items.prompt: <THE HOOK ITEM — the easiest, most instantly recognisable member of this theme. If item 1 makes a casual viewer feel behind, they are gone before item 2.>
<ITEM 2 — short, punchy, 1–2 words, the most instantly likeable thing in the theme. The one that makes a scroller smile, not the most 'useful' one.>
<ITEMS 3–9 — common, everyday, accessible. This is a light format, not a textbook: if a item feels advanced, swap it for an easier one.>

_itemRules: Hard cap ~44 characters per prompt and per answer; aim for ≤13 so each fits one clean centred line.
All items in one video must be distinct, and all must belong to the SAME theme. Never blend two themes in one video.

Broad, universally-appealing themes are worth MANY videos each with fresh items — 50 videos on a proven theme beats one on an obscure theme. Split a big theme into granular sub-themes so each video stays distinct.

_lineTemplate.prompt: <the spoken question, built from the item — same phrasing every time so the format is recognisable>
_lineTemplate.answer: <the spoken reveal; add a terminal full stop or the TTS clips it>

voiceOverlay._pronunciationTrap: When the written form and the spoken form differ (an abbreviation, a symbol, a non-phonetic script, a number), give the voice a separate spoken field. TTS reads the written form wrong and the audio then contradicts the screen — which is the one error viewers always comment on.

musicBackground._volumeRule: 3% under a voiceover. Anything louder fights the voice.

preflight._comment: Run before posting, not after. The invariant: what the voice says must match what's on screen. A batch that ships with mismatched audio is unrecoverable — every clip has to be re-rendered and re-posted.
checks: spoken text matches the on-screen reveal, item by item
no written form the TTS will read differently from the screen
grammatical agreement between prompt and answer (article, gender, number) — mismatches draw furious comments
no duplicate theme already sitting in the posting queue

_rules: Item 1 is the hook. Order the rest by how easy they are, not how useful.
Match the background to the theme.
Keep a record of what's been used so a viewer bingeing the series keeps getting new content — deliberately re-using a top performer is fine, drifting into repeats by accident is not.
